---
title: "Turn / BC onsets: when does the word matter beyond its POS?"
---

Is the word-level mode back (the most likely number of words left in the IU, given the word and its place) needed to predict backchannel (BC) and turn onsets, or is the POS-level one enough? And does the answer differ between onset types, IU types, or places in the IU? Instead of testing these one model at a time, every combination of the candidate predictors and their moderation is fitted and ranked by AIC ("Model selection"); the best model is interpreted with `marginaleffects` ("Main model"), and the robustness of the word-level effect across the candidate models is shown as a multiverse ("Robustness: multiverse"). All places are used, as in `turn_bc_gam_allplace.qmd`.

The step-by-step analyses that led to this, with Wald tests of differences between onset and IU types, are in `turn_bc_pos_moderators_steps.qmd`.

# Data

The packages, the model cache and output helpers, and the data are set up in `turn_bc_pos_moderators_data.R`, shared with `turn_bc_pos_moderators_steps.qmd`. The data are built as in `turn_bc_gam_allplace.qmd`: all places, words with a word-level and a POS-level mode back. The words of turns with a BC onset (outcome: BC onset on the word) and the words of turns with a turn onset (outcome: turn onset) are stacked (`stacked`), as the BC and turn models in `turn_bc_gam_allplace.qmd`; a word in a turn with both kinds of onset appears once in each half, and each half has its own document random intercepts. `cell` is onset type × IU type (terminal / non-terminal).

```{r}
source(here::here("nb", "turn_bc", "turn_bc_pos_moderators_data.R"))

# Words and onsets in each cell
read_csv(out_file("cell_counts.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# Model selection

All the models considered in `turn_bc_pos_moderators_steps.qmd` (and the POS section of `turn_bc_gam_allplace.qmd`) are points in one grid, so instead of reporting them one by one, every combination is fitted and ranked by AIC, and the best is the main model below.

Every model has the same backbone: an intercept and a place smooth for each cell (onset type × IU type), and document random intercepts for each onset type. On top of that, five choices:

| Choice | Values | Terms in the model |
|---|---|---|
| Expected remainder (3) | `word` | word-level `mode_back` |
| | `pos` | `mode_back_pos` |
| | `pos_word` | `mode_back_pos` + `modeback_diff` (= word-level `mode_back` split into its POS part and the word's deviation from it) |
| Actual remainder (3) | `none` | no actual remainder term |
| | `back` | actual `back` |
| | `err` | actual minus expected: `back - mode_back` for `word` and `pos_word`, `back - mode_back_pos` for `pos` |
| Form (2) | `linear` | one slope per term (per group, if moderated) |
| | `smooth` | a smooth per term (per group, if moderated); `k = 4` for `mode_back_pos`, `k = 6` otherwise. Applies to all the remainder terms of the model together |
| Moderation of the expected remainder terms (4) | `common` | one effect for all four cells |
| | `kind` | one effect per onset type (BC, turn), shared by terminal and non-terminal IUs |
| | `iu` | one effect per IU type (terminal, non-terminal), shared by BC and turn onsets |
| | `cell` | one effect per cell (onset type × IU type) |
| Moderation of the actual remainder term (4, or 1 when there is none) | same four values | as above, chosen independently of the moderation of the expected remainder |
| Interaction with place (4, or 2 when there is no actual remainder) | `none` | the remainder terms have the same effect at every place |
| | `expected` | the expected remainder terms interact with place |
| | `actual` | the actual remainder term interacts with place |
| | `both` | all the remainder terms interact with place |

An interaction with place has the same form and moderation as the term it belongs to: `ti(place, x, k = c(6, k))` (by group, if moderated) in the smooth models, which holds only the interaction, so the main effects are still those of `s(place)` and `s(x)`; `place:x` (by group) in the linear models.

The moderation of the actual remainder, and its interaction with place, only apply when there is an actual remainder term, so the count is:

| Actual remainder | Expected remainder | Form | Moderation (expected) | Moderation (actual) | Place interaction | Models |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `none` | 3 | 2 | 4 | 1 (none to moderate) | 2 (`none`, `expected`) | 3 × 2 × 4 × 2 = 48 |
| `back` | 3 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 3 × 2 × 4 × 4 × 4 = 384 |
| `err` | 3 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 3 × 2 × 4 × 4 × 4 = 384 |
| **Total** | | | | | | **816** |

All 816 are fitted to the same rows, so their conditional AICs are comparable. Some are the same model reparameterised (e.g. linear `back` and `err` with nested moderations); they have the same AIC and are marked in the ranking.

```{r}
k_default <- 6 # basis size for every smooth (per margin for ti())
# Basis size per variable: mode_back_pos takes too few values for k = 6
k_of <- c(
  mode_back = k_default,
  mode_back_pos = 4,
  modeback_diff = k_default,
  back = k_default,
  back_err = k_default,
  back_err_pos = k_default
)

# The variables of each choice of expected remainder
expectation_vars <- list(
  word = "mode_back", # word-level mode back
  pos = "mode_back_pos", # POS-level mode back
  pos_word = c("mode_back_pos", "modeback_diff") # POS-level plus the word's deviation from it
)
# The variable of each choice of actual remainder
remainder_var <- function(remainder, expectation) {
  switch(
    remainder,
    none = character(0), # no term
    back = "back", # actual back
    # Actual minus expected, relative to the expectation used in the model
    err = if (expectation == "pos") "back_err_pos" else "back_err"
  )
}

# One term for one variable, given its form and moderation
grid_term <- function(var, by, form) {
  if (form == "linear") {
    # One slope, or one slope per level of the moderator (e.g. "kind:back")
    if (by == "common") var else sprintf("%s:%s", by, var)
  } else if (by == "common") {
    sprintf("s(%s, k = %d)", var, k_of[[var]]) # one smooth
  } else {
    sprintf("s(%s, by = %s, k = %d)", var, by, k_of[[var]]) # one smooth per level of the moderator
  }
}

# Its interaction with place, with the same form and moderation (ti() holds
# only the interaction, so the main effects stay in s(place) and s(var))
grid_place_term <- function(var, by, form) {
  if (form == "linear") {
    if (by == "common") {
      sprintf("place:%s", var) # one place x variable slope
    } else {
      sprintf("%s:place:%s", by, var) # one per level of the moderator
    }
  } else {
    # Tensor-product interaction smooth, per level of the moderator if moderated
    sprintf(
      "ti(place, %s, %sk = c(%d, %d))",
      var,
      if (by == "common") "" else sprintf("by = %s, ", by),
      k_default, # basis size for place
      k_of[[var]] # basis size for the variable
    )
  }
}

# Every combination of the five choices, one row per model
model_grid <- expand_grid(
  expectation = names(expectation_vars),
  remainder = c("none", "back", "err"),
  form = c("linear", "smooth"),
  exp_by = c("common", "kind", "iu", "cell"),
  rem_by = c("common", "kind", "iu", "cell"),
  place_int = c("none", "expected", "actual", "both")
) %>%
  # Without an actual remainder there is nothing to moderate or interact with place
  filter(
    remainder != "none" |
      (rem_by == "common" & place_int %in% c("none", "expected"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rem_by = if_else(remainder == "none", NA_character_, rem_by), # NA when there's no actual remainder
    # Models without place interactions keep the ids they had before the
    # interactions were added, so their cached fits are reused
    id = paste0(
      paste(
        "grid",
        expectation,
        exp_by,
        remainder,
        coalesce(rem_by, "na"),
        form,
        sep = "_"
      ),
      if_else(place_int == "none", "", paste0("_pi-", place_int)) # e.g. "_pi-both"
    )
  )

# The formula of one grid row
grid_formula <- function(row) {
  # Expected remainder terms
  exp_terms <- vapply(
    expectation_vars[[row$expectation]],
    \(v) grid_term(v, row$exp_by, row$form),
    ""
  )
  # Actual remainder term (none if remainder is "none")
  rem_terms <- vapply(
    remainder_var(row$remainder, row$expectation),
    \(v) grid_term(v, row$rem_by, row$form),
    ""
  )
  # Place interactions of the expected remainder terms, if any (NULL otherwise)
  exp_place <- if (row$place_int %in% c("expected", "both")) {
    vapply(
      expectation_vars[[row$expectation]],
      \(v) grid_place_term(v, row$exp_by, row$form),
      ""
    )
  }
  # Place interaction of the actual remainder term, if any
  rem_place <- if (row$place_int %in% c("actual", "both")) {
    vapply(
      remainder_var(row$remainder, row$expectation),
      \(v) grid_place_term(v, row$rem_by, row$form),
      ""
    )
  }
  reformulate(
    c(
      "cell", # an intercept per cell
      sprintf("s(place, by = cell, k = %d)", k_default), # a place smooth per cell
      exp_terms,
      rem_terms,
      exp_place,
      rem_place,
      "s(docId, by = kind, bs = 're')" # document random intercepts per onset type
    ),
    response = "onset"
  )
}

nrow(model_grid) # 816
```

```{r}
# The fitted models are too big to keep all 816 in memory at once, so each one
# is fitted (or loaded from the cache), its AIC and edf are recorded, and it is
# dropped again. The recorded statistics are cached too (grid_stats.rds), so a
# re-render doesn't have to read every model file. Models needed later are read
# back from the cache with load_grid_model().
load_grid_model <- function(id) {
  readRDS(file.path(model_dir, paste0(id, ".rds")))
}

grid_stats_path <- file.path(model_dir, "grid_stats.rds") # cached AIC / edf per model
grid_stats <- if (!refit_models && file.exists(grid_stats_path)) {
  readRDS(grid_stats_path)
} else {
  tibble(
    id = character(),
    formula = character(),
    edf = numeric(),
    AIC = numeric()
  )
}

for (i in seq_len(nrow(model_grid))) {
  row <- model_grid[i, ]
  f <- grid_formula(row)
  f_text <- deparse1(f) # formula as text, to check the cached statistics against
  # Skip models whose statistics are already recorded for this formula
  if (any(grid_stats$id == row$id & grid_stats$formula == f_text)) {
    next
  }
  m <- fit_or_load(
    row$id,
    bam(
      f,
      data = stacked,
      family = binomial(link = "logit"), # onset (TRUE / FALSE) on the log-odds scale
      method = "fREML", # fast REML for the smoothing parameters
      discrete = TRUE # discretised covariates, for speed
    ),
    formula = f # refit if the cached model's formula differs
  )
  # Record the model's statistics, replacing any for an older formula
  grid_stats <- grid_stats %>%
    filter(id != row$id) %>%
    bind_rows(tibble(
      id = row$id,
      formula = f_text,
      edf = sum(m$edf), # effective degrees of freedom
      AIC = AIC(m) # conditional AIC
    ))
  rm(m) # drop the model before the next one
  gc()
  saveRDS(grid_stats, grid_stats_path) # save as we go, in case the run is interrupted
}

ranking <- model_grid %>%
  left_join(grid_stats, by = "id") %>% # AIC, edf and formula of each model
  arrange(AIC) %>%
  arrange(AIC) %>% # best first
  mutate(
    dAIC = AIC - min(AIC), # difference from the best
    # Reparameterisations of the same model have the same AIC
    same_fit_as = map_chr(seq_along(AIC), \(i) {
      # An earlier (better or equal) model with the same AIC, if any
      j <- which(abs(AIC[seq_len(i - 1)] - AIC[i]) < 1e-4)
      if (length(j)) id[j[1]] else NA_character_
    })
  )

invisible(save_table(ranking, "grid_ranking")) # the full ranking (saved, not printed)

# The ten best distinct models
ranking %>%
  filter(is.na(same_fit_as)) %>%
  select(expectation, exp_by, remainder, rem_by, form, place_int, edf, dAIC) %>%
  head(10)
```

Summary for reporting: the best model for each choice of expected and actual remainder (other choices free), as ΔAIC from the overall best.

```{r}
best_by <- ranking %>%
  group_by(expectation, remainder) %>% # each combination of expected and actual remainder
  slice_min(AIC, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% # its best model
  ungroup() %>%
  select(expectation, remainder, exp_by, rem_by, form, place_int, dAIC) %>%
  arrange(dAIC)

save_table(best_by, "grid_best_by_choice")
best_by
```

And the best model for each choice of interaction with place:

```{r}
best_by_place <- ranking %>%
  group_by(place_int) %>% # each choice of interaction with place
  slice_min(AIC, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% # its best model
  ungroup() %>%
  select(place_int, expectation, remainder, exp_by, rem_by, form, dAIC) %>%
  arrange(dAIC)

save_table(best_by_place, "grid_best_by_place_interaction")
best_by_place
```

# Main model

The model with the lowest AIC in the grid.

```{r}
best <- ranking[1, ] # the row of the best model
m_main <- load_grid_model(best$id) # the model itself, from the cache
# Its remainder variables
main_vars <- c(
  expectation_vars[[best$expectation]],
  remainder_var(best$remainder, best$expectation)
)

best %>%
  select(expectation, exp_by, remainder, rem_by, form, place_int, edf, AIC)
save_text(summary(m_main), "main_model_summary")
summary(m_main)
```

The main results are the fitted curves: predicted P(onset) against each remainder term, by cell, at three places in the IU (`main_places`; the curves differ in shape between places only if the term interacts with place), with the other terms at their means and the document effects left out (`exclude = "s(docId)"`), from `marginaleffects::predictions()`. The grid sets `kind` and `iu` to match each `cell` (left to themselves, `datagrid()` would hold them at their most common values, and every cell would get the turn smooths), and each term runs over its 1st to 99th percentile, as the curves are poorly constrained in the sparse tails.

```{r}
library(marginaleffects) # predictions() / slopes() from fitted models

# Prediction / slope grid with kind and iu consistent with cell
cell_grid <- function(model, ...) {
  # One row per cell, with every other variable at its mean (or most common value)
  g <- datagrid(model = model, cell = levels(stacked$cell), ...)
  # Set kind and iu from the cell, e.g. "bc_terminal" -> bc, terminal
  g$kind <- factor(
    str_remove(as.character(g$cell), "_.*"),
    levels(stacked$kind)
  )
  g$iu <- factor(str_remove(as.character(g$cell), ".*_"), levels(stacked$iu))
  g
}

main_places <- c(1, 3, 6) # places at which the curves and slopes are shown

# Moderation of a variable's effect in the main model (its place interaction,
# if any, has the same moderation)
moderation_of <- function(v) {
  if (v %in% expectation_vars[[best$expectation]]) best$exp_by else best$rem_by
}
# Whether the main model gives these variables the same effect in terminal and
# non-terminal IUs; if so, the two IU types are lumped in the plots
lump_iu <- function(vars) {
  all(vapply(vars, moderation_of, "") %in% c("common", "kind"))
}

# Each onset type's share of words in each IU type, the weights for averaging
# predictions over IU types
iu_share <- stacked %>%
  count(kind, iu) %>%
  group_by(kind) %>%
  mutate(w = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(kind, iu, w)

# Grid of each cell x each place x each row of `values` (a data frame of the
# varied variables), everything else at its mean
value_grid <- function(values) {
  g <- cell_grid(m_main)
  tidyr::expand_grid(
    g[setdiff(names(g), c(names(values), "place"))],
    place = main_places,
    values %>% mutate(value_id = row_number()) # to match results back to values
  )
}

# Predictions over value_grid(values). With lump = TRUE they are averaged over
# the two IU types within each onset type (weighted by iu_share), and iu is
# "both"; otherwise there is one prediction per cell.
grid_predictions <- function(values, lump, type) {
  g <- value_grid(values)
  if (lump) {
    g <- g %>%
      left_join(iu_share, by = c("kind", "iu")) %>% # weight of each row
      mutate(grp_id = paste(kind, place, value_id, sep = "|")) # rows to average
    pr <- predictions(
      m_main,
      newdata = g,
      by = "grp_id", # average within onset type, place and value ...
      wts = "w", # ... weighted by the IU types' shares
      exclude = "s(docId)", # leave out the document effects
      type = type
    ) %>%
      as.data.frame()
    g %>%
      distinct(grp_id, kind, place, value_id) %>%
      left_join(values %>% mutate(value_id = row_number()), by = "value_id") %>%
      left_join(
        pr %>% select(grp_id, estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
        by = "grp_id"
      ) %>%
      mutate(onset = as.character(kind), iu = "both") %>%
      select(
        onset,
        iu,
        place,
        all_of(names(values)),
        estimate,
        conf.low,
        conf.high
      )
  } else {
    pr <- predictions(
      m_main,
      newdata = g,
      exclude = "s(docId)", # leave out the document effects
      type = type
    ) %>%
      as.data.frame()
    stopifnot(nrow(pr) == nrow(g)) # one prediction per grid row, in order
    # Take the grid values from the grid itself
    g %>%
      transmute(
        onset = as.character(kind),
        iu = as.character(iu),
        place,
        across(all_of(names(values))),
        estimate = pr$estimate,
        conf.low = pr$conf.low,
        conf.high = pr$conf.high
      )
  }
}

# Slopes of v over value_grid(values), on the log-odds scale. With lump = TRUE
# the terminal rows are used and iu is "both": on the log-odds scale a variable
# whose effect doesn't depend on the IU type has exactly the same slope in both.
grid_slopes <- function(v, values, lump) {
  g <- value_grid(values)
  if (lump) {
    g <- g %>% filter(iu == "terminal")
  }
  s <- slopes(
    m_main,
    variables = v, # derivative with respect to this variable
    newdata = g,
    exclude = "s(docId)", # leave out the document effects
    type = "link" # log-odds scale
  ) %>%
    as.data.frame()
  # One row per grid row, in order; the output's copy of the focal variable
  # isn't the grid value, so take it from the grid
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == nrow(g))
  g %>%
    transmute(
      onset = as.character(kind),
      iu = if (lump) "both" else as.character(iu),
      place,
      across(all_of(names(values))),
      estimate = s$estimate,
      std.error = s$std.error,
      conf.low = s$conf.low,
      conf.high = s$conf.high,
      p.value = s$p.value
    )
}

# Values of a variable for the curves: 60 points over its 1st to 99th percentile
curve_values <- function(v) {
  rng <- quantile(stacked[[v]], c(0.01, 0.99))
  tibble(!!v := seq(rng[[1]], rng[[2]], length.out = 60))
}

# Range of each variable with data at each place: from the smallest to the
# largest whole-number value that at least 100 words within one place have.
# The curves are cut to these ranges, so they don't show the model
# extrapolating into values that hardly occur at that place (e.g. large
# modeback_diff values, which are almost all IU-initial).
supported_range <- lapply(main_vars, \(v) {
  lapply(main_places, \(p) {
    stacked %>%
      filter(abs(place - p) <= 1) %>%
      count(value = floor(.data[[v]] + 0.5)) %>%
      filter(n >= 100) %>%
      summarise(lo = min(value) - 0.5, hi = max(value) + 0.5) %>%
      mutate(term = v, place = p)
  }) %>%
    bind_rows()
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

# Keep the parts of the curves within the supported range at each place
cut_to_support <- function(curves) {
  curves %>%
    left_join(supported_range, by = c("term", "place")) %>%
    filter(x >= lo, x <= hi) %>%
    select(-lo, -hi)
}

# Predicted P(onset) against each remainder variable
main_curves <- lapply(main_vars, \(v) {
  grid_predictions(curve_values(v), lump = lump_iu(v), type = "response") %>%
    mutate(term = v, x = .data[[v]]) %>%
    select(term, onset, iu, place, x, estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  cut_to_support()

# One plot per variable: colour = onset type, line type = IU type, panels = place
for (v in main_vars) {
  p <- main_curves %>%
    filter(term == v) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x, estimate, colour = onset, fill = onset, linetype = iu)) +
    geom_ribbon(
      # 95% CI
      aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
      alpha = 0.12,
      colour = NA
    ) +
    geom_line() + # predicted P(onset)
    facet_wrap(~place, labeller = label_both, scales = "free_y") + # one panel per place
    labs(
      x = v,
      y = "P(onset)",
      colour = "Onset",
      fill = "Onset",
      linetype = "IU"
    )
  print(save_plot(p, paste0("main_predictions_", v), width = 11, height = 4.5))
}
```

The first derivatives of the same curves: the slope of each term (log-odds per word, from `slopes()`) along its range, by cell and place, with 95% confidence bands. Where a band excludes 0, P(onset) is reliably changing with the term at that value. They are on the log-odds scale, where (unlike on the probability scale) a term's slope doesn't depend on the values of the other terms.

```{r}
# Slope of each remainder variable along its range (same values as main_curves)
main_derivs <- lapply(main_vars, \(v) {
  grid_slopes(v, curve_values(v), lump = lump_iu(v)) %>%
    mutate(term = v, x = .data[[v]]) %>%
    select(term, onset, iu, place, x, estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  cut_to_support() # same supported ranges as the curves

invisible(save_table(main_derivs, "main_derivatives")) # saved, not printed

# One plot per variable, in the same style as the prediction curves
for (v in main_vars) {
  p <- main_derivs %>%
    filter(term == v) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x, estimate, colour = onset, fill = onset, linetype = iu)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + # zero slope
    geom_ribbon(
      # 95% CI
      aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
      alpha = 0.12,
      colour = NA
    ) +
    geom_line() + # the slope
    facet_wrap(~place, labeller = label_both) + # one panel per place, same y scale
    labs(
      x = v,
      y = "Slope (log-odds per word)",
      colour = "Onset",
      fill = "Onset",
      linetype = "IU"
    )
  print(save_plot(p, paste0("main_derivatives_", v), width = 11, height = 4.5))
}
```

When the main model has both the POS-level mode back and the word's deviation from it, the two together: P(onset) against `mode_back_pos`, with a line for each of several values of `modeback_diff`, so the size of the word-level shifts can be read against the POS-level effect. A combination of the two is only shown at a place if at least 100 words within one place of it have it (some can't occur at all, e.g. `mode_back_pos` = 1 with `modeback_diff` = −1 would be a word-level mode back of 0, and words with large differences are almost all IU-initial). Actual back is at its mean and the document effects are left out.

```{r}
# Combinations of mode_back_pos and modeback_diff that at least 100 words have
# within one place of each of main_places
supported_by_place <- lapply(main_places, \(p) {
  stacked %>%
    filter(abs(place - p) <= 1) %>%
    count(mode_back_pos, modeback_diff) %>%
    filter(n >= 100) %>%
    mutate(place = p)
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

# Only if the main model has both terms
if (all(c("mode_back_pos", "modeback_diff") %in% main_vars)) {
  diff_values <- -1:2 # values of modeback_diff to draw (about 90% of the words)
  # Every combination supported at any of the places
  combos <- supported_by_place %>%
    filter(modeback_diff %in% diff_values) %>%
    distinct(mode_back_pos, modeback_diff)

  pos_by_diff <- grid_predictions(
    combos,
    lump = lump_iu(c("mode_back_pos", "modeback_diff")),
    type = "response" # probability scale
  ) %>%
    # Keep each combination only at the places where it is supported
    semi_join(
      supported_by_place,
      by = c("place", "mode_back_pos", "modeback_diff")
    ) %>%
    mutate(modeback_diff = factor(modeback_diff)) # a factor, for the colour scale

  save_table(pos_by_diff, "main_predictions_pos_by_diff")

  # x = POS-level mode back, colour = word minus POS; rows = cells, columns = places
  p <- ggplot(
    pos_by_diff,
    aes(mode_back_pos, estimate, colour = modeback_diff, group = modeback_diff)
  ) +
    geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.25)) +
    geom_pointrange(
      # 95% CI
      aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.25),
      size = 0.25
    ) +
    facet_grid(
      onset + iu ~ place,
      scales = "free_y",
      labeller = labeller(place = label_both)
    ) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85) +
    labs(
      x = "POS-level mode back (mode_back_pos)",
      y = "P(onset)",
      colour = "Word minus POS\n(modeback_diff)"
    )
  print(save_plot(p, "main_predictions_pos_by_diff", width = 10, height = 9))
}
```

The joint effect of the two as a contour plot: the change in log-odds of an onset relative to a word with `mode_back_pos` = 1 and `modeback_diff` = 0, in the same cell and at the same place (so the cells' different base rates don't swamp the shape, and all panels share one colour scale). At each place, only the area around combinations that at least 100 words within one place of it have is shown; the dots mark those combinations, sized by the number of words. When the two terms don't depend on the IU type in the main model, terminal and non-terminal IUs are shown as one: on the log-odds scale they then differ only by a constant, which the change from the reference removes.

```{r}
# Only if the main model has both terms
if (all(c("mode_back_pos", "modeback_diff") %in% main_vars)) {
  lump <- lump_iu(c("mode_back_pos", "modeback_diff"))
  # A fine grid over the two variables, covering the combinations supported at any place
  pos_range <- range(supported_by_place$mode_back_pos)
  diff_range <- range(supported_by_place$modeback_diff)
  fine <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    mode_back_pos = seq(pos_range[1], pos_range[2], length.out = 61),
    modeback_diff = seq(diff_range[1], diff_range[2], length.out = 141)
  )
  g <- value_grid(fine)
  # Lumped: the terminal rows stand for both IU types (same change from the reference)
  if (lump) {
    g <- g %>% filter(iu == "terminal")
  }
  pr <- predictions(
    m_main,
    newdata = g,
    exclude = "s(docId)", # leave out the document effects
    type = "link" # log-odds scale
  ) %>%
    as.data.frame()
  stopifnot(nrow(pr) == nrow(g)) # one prediction per grid row, in order

  joint <- g %>%
    transmute(
      onset = as.character(kind),
      iu = if (lump) "both" else as.character(iu),
      place,
      mode_back_pos,
      modeback_diff,
      eta = pr$estimate # predicted log-odds
    ) %>%
    # Nearest whole-number combination of each grid point
    mutate(
      pos_near = floor(mode_back_pos + 0.5),
      diff_near = floor(modeback_diff + 0.5)
    ) %>%
    # Keep grid points whose nearest combination is supported at that place
    semi_join(
      supported_by_place,
      by = c("place", pos_near = "mode_back_pos", diff_near = "modeback_diff")
    ) %>%
    group_by(onset, iu, place) %>%
    # Change in log-odds from mode_back_pos = 1, modeback_diff = 0 in the same cell and place
    mutate(
      delta = eta -
        eta[which.min(abs(mode_back_pos - 1) + abs(modeback_diff - 0))]
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  supported <- supported_by_place # the dots, by place

  save_table(joint, "main_joint_pos_diff")

  p <- ggplot(joint, aes(mode_back_pos, modeback_diff)) +
    geom_raster(aes(fill = delta)) + # the change in log-odds
    geom_contour(
      aes(z = delta),
      breaks = seq(-3, 3, by = 0.2), # a contour every 0.2 log-odds
      colour = "grey30",
      linewidth = 0.25
    ) +
    geom_point(
      # the supported combinations, sized by number of words
      data = supported,
      aes(size = n),
      shape = 21,
      fill = NA,
      colour = "grey20"
    ) +
    facet_grid(
      onset + iu ~ place,
      labeller = labeller(place = label_both)
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      # blue = less likely, red = more likely than the reference
      low = "#2a78d6",
      mid = "white",
      high = "#e34948",
      midpoint = 0
    ) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 3) +
    coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) +
    labs(
      x = "POS-level mode back (mode_back_pos)",
      y = "Word minus POS (modeback_diff)",
      fill = "Change in\nlog-odds\nfrom (1, 0)",
      size = "Words"
    )
  print(save_plot(p, "main_joint_pos_diff", width = 10, height = 10))
}
```

Slopes at a few values of each term (log-odds per word, from `slopes()`), rather than an average slope: with curved smooths an average over each cell's words mixes the steep and flat parts of the curve in proportions that differ between cells. The values cover the bulk of the data (roughly the 5th to 95th percentile; `modeback_diff` is 0 for over half of the words). On the log-odds scale a term's slope at a given value doesn't depend on the other terms, and doesn't depend on place either unless the term interacts with place; the slopes are shown at the same three places as the curves. Cells that share a smooth (e.g. terminal and non-terminal IUs, where a term is moderated by onset type only) have the same slopes.

```{r}
# Values at which each variable's slope is computed
slope_points <- list(
  modeback_diff = -2:3,
  mode_back_pos = 1:4,
  back = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9),
  back_err = -4:4,
  back_err_pos = -4:6,
  mode_back = 1:5
)

# Slope of each remainder variable at those values, in each cell, at each place
main_point_slopes <- lapply(main_vars, \(v) {
  grid_slopes(v, tibble(!!v := slope_points[[v]]), lump = lump_iu(v)) %>%
    mutate(term = v, value = .data[[v]]) %>%
    select(
      term,
      onset,
      iu,
      place,
      value,
      estimate,
      std.error,
      conf.low,
      conf.high,
      p.value
    )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

invisible(save_table(main_point_slopes, "main_point_slopes")) # saved, not printed

# Slope against the variable's value; rows = places, columns = variables
p <- ggplot(
  main_point_slopes,
  aes(value, estimate, colour = onset, shape = iu)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + # zero slope
  geom_pointrange(
    # 95% CI
    aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
    size = 0.3
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    place ~ term,
    scales = "free_x",
    labeller = labeller(place = label_both)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Value of the term",
    y = "Slope (log-odds per word)",
    colour = "Onset",
    shape = "IU"
  )
save_plot(p, "main_point_slopes", width = 10, height = 8)
```

# Robustness: multiverse

Does the word-level mode back predict onsets beyond the actual remainder and the POS-level mode back, in each cell, whichever model is used? The question is defined in the 128 grid models with `mode_back_pos` + `modeback_diff` and actual back (32 combinations of form and moderation, each with the four choices of interaction with place) (in the `err` models the `modeback_diff` effect includes the effect of the actual remainder moving with it, so it answers a different question). For each of them, the effect is the slope of `modeback_diff` in each cell at `modeback_diff` = −1, 0, 1 and 2 (about 90% of the words) and at the median place (`multiverse_place`; this only matters in models where the expected remainder interacts with place), on the log-odds scale (`slopes()`, document effects excluded), which puts linear and smooth fits on the same footing; in the linear models the four values have the same slope. The models are ordered by AIC and shown with their Akaike weights in the full grid (Steegen et al. 2016; Simonsohn, Simmons & Nelson 2020).

The 128 estimates come from the same data, so they are not independent tests; the point is whether the conclusion depends on the specification, not how many of them are significant.

```{r}
library(patchwork) # stacking ggplots with /

# Akaike weights over the distinct fits in the whole grid
weights <- ranking %>%
  filter(is.na(same_fit_as)) %>% # each distinct model once
  mutate(weight = exp(-dAIC / 2) / sum(exp(-dAIC / 2))) %>% # relative likelihood, normalised
  select(id, weight)

# The models in which the question is defined: POS + word minus POS, with actual back
multiverse_specs <- ranking %>%
  filter(expectation == "pos_word", remainder == "back") %>%
  left_join(weights, by = "id") %>%
  mutate(
    weight = coalesce(weight, 0), # reparameterised duplicates get no weight of their own
    place_int = factor(place_int, c("none", "expected", "actual", "both"))
  ) %>%
  # Ordered by AIC within each choice of interaction with place
  group_by(place_int) %>%
  mutate(spec_rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

multiverse_points <- -1:2 # values of modeback_diff at which the slope is taken
multiverse_place <- median(stacked$place) # place at which the slope is taken

# Cached, as computing the slopes for all these models takes a while
multiverse_path <- file.path(model_dir, "multiverse_point_slopes_v3.rds")
multiverse_slopes <- if (!refit_models && file.exists(multiverse_path)) {
  readRDS(multiverse_path)
} else {
  NULL
}
# Recompute if there is no cache, or it is for a different set of models / fits
if (
  is.null(multiverse_slopes) ||
    !setequal(unique(multiverse_slopes$id), multiverse_specs$id) ||
    !identical(
      multiverse_slopes %>% distinct(id, AIC) %>% arrange(id) %>% pull(AIC),
      multiverse_specs %>% arrange(id) %>% pull(AIC)
    )
) {
  # For each model, the slope of modeback_diff at each value, in each cell
  multiverse_slopes <- lapply(multiverse_specs$id, \(x) {
    m <- load_grid_model(x) # one model at a time, from the cache
    grid <- cell_grid(m)
    # Each cell x each value of modeback_diff, at the median place
    grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
      grid[setdiff(names(grid), c("modeback_diff", "place"))],
      place = multiverse_place,
      modeback_diff = multiverse_points
    )
    s <- slopes(
      m,
      variables = "modeback_diff",
      newdata = grid,
      exclude = "s(docId)", # leave out the document effects
      type = "link" # log-odds scale
    ) %>%
      as.data.frame()
    # One row per grid row, in order (see main_point_slopes above)
    stopifnot(nrow(s) == nrow(grid))
    s %>%
      mutate(cell = grid$cell, value = grid$modeback_diff) %>%
      transmute(
        id = x,
        AIC = AIC(m), # stored to check the cache against later
        cell,
        value,
        estimate,
        conf.low,
        conf.high,
        p.value
      )
  }) %>%
    bind_rows()
  saveRDS(multiverse_slopes, multiverse_path)
}

# The slopes with each model's choices, rank and weight
multiverse <- multiverse_slopes %>%
  select(-AIC) %>%
  left_join(multiverse_specs, by = "id") %>%
  separate(cell, c("onset", "iu"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(excludes_zero = conf.high < 0 | conf.low > 0) # whether the 95% CI excludes 0

invisible(save_table(
  multiverse %>%
    select(
      place_int,
      spec_rank,
      id,
      form,
      exp_by,
      rem_by,
      dAIC,
      weight,
      cell,
      value,
      estimate,
      conf.low,
      conf.high,
      p.value
    ),
  "multiverse_slopes"
)) # saved, not printed
```

```{r}
# Estimates by specification, one row of panels per cell and one column per
# choice of interaction with place (ordered by AIC within each); the values of
# modeback_diff are side by side within each specification. The three stacked
# plots have the same columns and x axes, so a column of points is one
# specification.
spec_x <- scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) # same x axis in all three plots
int_labels <- labeller(place_int = \(x) paste("place interaction:", x)) # column titles

# Top: the slope estimates
p_est <- multiverse %>%
  mutate(
    value = factor(value), # a factor, for the colour scale
    ci = if_else(excludes_zero, "CI excludes 0", "CI includes 0")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(spec_rank, estimate, colour = value, shape = ci)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + # zero slope
  geom_pointrange(
    # estimate and 95% CI
    aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), # the four values side by side
    size = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    onset + iu ~ place_int, # rows = cells, columns = place interaction
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free_x",
    labeller = int_labels
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("CI excludes 0" = 16, "CI includes 0" = 1)) + # filled / open
  spec_x +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Slope of modeback_diff (log-odds per word)",
    colour = "At modeback_diff =",
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")

# Middle: each model's Akaike weight
p_weight <- multiverse_specs %>%
  ggplot(aes(spec_rank, weight)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(. ~ place_int, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") + # same columns as above
  spec_x +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Akaike\nweight") +
  theme(strip.text = element_blank()) + # column titles only on the top plot
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

# Bottom: each model's choices
p_spec <- multiverse_specs %>%
  transmute(
    place_int,
    spec_rank,
    form = form,
    `expected remainder` = exp_by,
    `actual back` = rem_by
  ) %>%
  # One row per model and choice
  pivot_longer(
    -c(place_int, spec_rank),
    names_to = "choice",
    values_to = "option"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(spec_rank, option)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) + # a dot at the option each model takes
  facet_grid(
    choice ~ place_int,
    scales = "free",
    space = "free",
    switch = "y"
  ) +
  spec_x +
  labs(
    x = "Specification (best AIC on the left, within each column)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.x = element_blank())

p <- p_est / p_weight / p_spec + plot_layout(heights = c(8, 1, 3)) # stack the three
save_plot(p, "multiverse", width = 18, height = 11)
```

Summary per cell and value of `modeback_diff`: the range of estimates, how many intervals exclude 0, and the Akaike-weighted average estimate (weights renormalised over the models in each column). The full table is saved to `multiverse_summary.csv`; only the rows for `modeback_diff` = 0 (over half of the words) are printed:

```{r}
multiverse %>%
  group_by(place_int, onset, iu, value) %>%
  summarise(
    specifications = n(), # number of models
    min_estimate = min(estimate), # range of the estimates
    max_estimate = max(estimate),
    n_negative = sum(estimate < 0), # how many are negative
    n_ci_excludes_zero = sum(excludes_zero), # how many CIs exclude 0
    weighted_estimate = sum(weight * estimate) / sum(weight), # Akaike-weighted mean
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  save_table("multiverse_summary") %>%
  filter(value == 0) # print only these rows
```
